claims.text: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The prisma.workflowReminder.update newly added inside the catch block is itself unprotected; if it throws (P2025 when the row was already deleted, or the DB being unavailable — the very reason the catch ran), the exception escapes the for loop and the whole cron run turns into a 500, escalating a single-reminder failure into a run-wide one.

The deletion is silent: deleteMany's count is not even captured, no reminder id is logged, and the existing console.log does not include the reminder id or use the repo's logger, so afterwards there is no way to answer which reminders were abandoned or why.

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

The newly added data-deleting branch has no tests at all — there are no test files under packages/features/ee/workflows — even though the repo already uses prismock to test SMS lock behaviour, so the tooling exists.
`gt: 1` is an unnamed, uncommented threshold; it should be a named constant (e.g. MAX_SMS_SCHEDULE_ATTEMPTS) so the intended limit is explicit.
`update()` will throw if the reminder was deleted between `findMany` and this write, which would escape the catch block - needs to be robust to concurrency and missing rows

The Twilio provider API call and database persistence are in a single try-catch, so if Twilio accepts the SMS but the database update fails, the error is treated as a send failure causing duplicate SMS on retry
After multiple database failures, the reminder row may be deleted leaving orphaned jobs on Twilio with no database reference

The prisma.workflowReminder.update in the catch block (line 191) is unprotected - if it throws (e.g., the record was already deleted by the deleteMany above, or a DB connection issue), the error propagates out of the for...of loop and halts processing of all remaining reminders. Wrap this update in a nested try-catch or append .catch() to prevent a single failure from stopping the entire cron job.

Unguarded DB write inside catch block - if prisma.workflowReminder.update throws (e.g. network issue, record already deleted), the error will propagate out of the catch and abort the entire for loop, leaving subsequent reminders unprocessed

What does this deleteMany actually cost in production every 15 minutes? The retryCount branch has no usable index, and neither the DB nor production row counts are available here to tell whether this is negligible or a recurring full table scan.

Because the OR combines an indexed predicate with retryCount, for which there is no index, the whole deleteMany can no longer use the @@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate]) and runs every 15 minutes without index support.

After only two failed scheduling attempts (about 30 minutes) the reminder row is permanently deleted, even though the event may still be up to 7 days away and the delete branch has no scheduledDate condition; the failures that increment the counter are mostly transient or environmental (missing Twilio credentials, Twilio outage, SMS lock), and nothing ever recreates the deleted reminder.

Are the WhatsApp and Email crons deliberately out of scope, or were they missed? retryCount lives on the shared WorkflowReminder model but only the SMS cron uses it, and scheduleWhatsappReminders is nearly identical with the same unbounded retrying.

The field is named retryCount but becomes 1 after the first attempt, which is not a retry, so the name is off by one from the semantics (failureCount would be accurate) — an easy target for someone later 'fixing' it to gte: 1 or gt: 2.
